q: 1. On which date was the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) officially established?
explain: SAARC was established on December 8, 1985, with the signing of the SAARC Charter during the 1st Summit in Dhaka, Bangladesh. May 2, 1980 is when regional cooperation was first proposed; January 16, 1987 is when the Secretariat was founded in Kathmandu; April 4, 2007 is when Afghanistan joined at the 14th Summit.

q: 2. What do the seven pigeons in the official SAARC logo represent?
explain: The seven doves nestled between the hands represent the original seven founding member countries seeking regional peace. Objectives refers to Article I (8 objectives); organs refers to the structural framework; agreements refers to trade treaties like SAPTA, SAFTA, and SATIS.

q: 3. Under which Article of the United Nations Charter are regional organizations like SAARC established?
explain: Article 52 of the UN Charter permits regional arrangements to maintain international peace and security. Article 51 deals with self-defense; Article 111 is the closing article of the UN Charter; Article 19 governs voting rights.

q: 4. The cow is the national animal of which SAARC country?
explain: The cow is the national animal of Nepal. India and Bangladesh have tigers as national animals; Sri Lanka has the lion.

q: 5. Which Article of the SAARC Charter governs the Summit meetings of the Heads of State or Government?
explain: Article III mandates that meetings of Heads of State or Government shall be held once every two years (Summit). Articles IV, V, and X cover other organs and general provisions.

q: 6. Which Article of the SAARC Charter defines the composition and functions of the Council of Ministers?
explain: Article IV outlines the Council of Ministers (Foreign Ministers), their duties, and bi-annual meetings. Articles III, V, and VI govern other bodies.

q: 7. The Standing Committee of Foreign Secretaries is established under which Article of the SAARC Charter?
explain: Article V establishes the Standing Committee of Foreign Secretaries. Articles IV, VI, and VII govern other committees.

q: 8. The financial arrangements and voluntary contributions of SAARC are detailed under which Article?
explain: Article IX covers financial arrangements, voluntary budget allocations, and Secretariat expenditures. Article VIII covers administration.

q: 9. How many core objectives are defined under Article I of the SAARC Charter?
explain: Article I contains exactly 8 specific objectives. Three is the number of principles; Seven is the number of founding states.

q: 10. Who was the first Secretary-General of SAARC?
explain: Abul Ahsan of Bangladesh was appointed the first Secretary-General, serving from 1987 to 1989. Yadav Kant Silwal was 4th, Kant Kishore Bhargava was 2nd, and Ibrahim Hussein Zaki was 3rd.

q: 11. Which country does the current Secretary-General of SAARC, Golam Sarwar, represent?
explain: Current Secretary-General Golam Sarwar represents Bangladesh. The other options are other member states.

q: 12. Which member state pays the largest voluntary contribution share (30.32%) to the SAARC budget?
explain: India contributes the largest share (30.32%) to the voluntary budget. Pakistan pays 22.52%; Bangladesh and Nepal pay 10.72%.

q: 13. Which three countries contribute exactly 10.72% each to the SAARC budget?
explain: These three nations contribute exactly 10.72% each. The other options feature different percentage brackets.

q: 14. In which country was the historic First SAARC Summit held in December 1985?
explain: The 1st SAARC Summit was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on December 7-8, 1985. The other options hosted later summits.

q: 15. Who was the first Prime Minister of Nepal to represent the country in a SAARC Summit (5th Summit, 1990)?
explain: Prime Minister KP Bhattarai represented Nepal at the 5th Summit in Male (1990). The other options represented Nepal at later summits.

q: 16. Which Prime Minister represented Nepal at the 11th SAARC Summit held in Kathmandu in January 2002?
explain: PM Deuba represented Nepal at the 11th Summit in Kathmandu (2002). The other options are other Prime Ministers who attended different summits.

q: 17. Which scheduled SAARC Summit was cancelled following the Uri Attack and India's subsequent withdrawal?
explain: The 19th Summit, scheduled for Islamabad in 2016, was cancelled due to the Uri Attack and India's withdrawal. The other options were held successfully.

q: 18. How many Articles are there in the charter of SAFTA?
explain: SAFTA, like SAPTA, contains exactly 25 Articles in its charter. The other options do not represent the correct article count.

q: 19. During which summit was the SAARC Agreement on Trade in Services (SATIS) signed in April 2010?
explain: SATIS was signed during the 16th Summit in Thimphu, Bhutan, in April 2010. The other options hosted different summit frameworks.

q: 20. Where is the Secretariat of the South Asian Regional Standards Organization (SARSO) located?
explain: SARSO (Standards Organization) has its permanent Secretariat in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The other options host other specialized institutions.

q: 21. Which intergovernmental body of SAARC is located in Islamabad, Pakistan to provide a forum for commercial and trade dispute resolution?
explain: The Arbitration Council is located in Islamabad, Pakistan, for legal dispute resolution. The other options are based in other member capitals.

q: 22. Which is the oldest regional center of SAARC, established in 1989?
explain: SAC is the oldest center, established in 1989 in Dhaka. STAC was established in 1992, SEC in 2006, and SCC in 2009.

q: 23. Where is the SAARC TB and HIV/AIDS Centre (STAC) located?
explain: STAC is located in Bhaktapur, Nepal. Kathmandu and Pokhara are other Nepalese cities; Dhaka is in Bangladesh.

q: 24. In which year was the SAARC TB Centre established, which was later renamed STAC in November 2007?
explain: The SAARC TB Centre started functioning in 1994 and was renamed STAC in November 2007. 1989 is SAC's year, 1992 is STAC's regional center establishment year, and 2006 is SEC's establishment year.

q: 25. What is the cash prize associated with the SAARC Award established in 2004?
explain: The SAARC Award cash prize is $25,000 (USD) along with a certificate. The other options are incorrect prize amounts.

q: 26. Who was first raised the concept of regional, political and economical cooperation in South Asia?
explain: President Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh is credited with first proposing the idea of regional cooperation in South Asia in the late 1970s.

q: 27. Which of the following given is/are the principles of SAARC?
explain: Article II of the SAARC Charter lists sovereign equality, territorial integrity, and non-interference in internal affairs among its guiding principles.

q: 28. In which Article of the SAARC Charter, the principles of the SAARC is mentioned?
explain: Article II of the SAARC Charter lays down the guiding principles of the organization.

q: 29. Which country is not the founder member of the SAARC?
explain: SAARC was founded in 1985 by seven countries; Afghanistan joined later, in 2007, becoming the eighth member.

q: 30. When was the 18th Summit of SAARC in Kathmandu held?
explain: The 18th SAARC Summit was held in Kathmandu, Nepal from 26-27 November 2014.

q: 31. When was SAARC framework agreement for energy Co-operation signed on?
explain: The SAARC Framework Agreement on Energy Cooperation was signed on 27 November 2014 during the 18th Summit in Kathmandu.

q: 32. SAARC is observing a decade (2010-2020) of which of the following?
explain: SAARC declared 2010-2020 as the Decade of Intra-regional Connectivity to strengthen physical, economic, and people-to-people links.

q: 33. What was the theme of the SAARC year 2016-17 A.D.?
explain: SAARC observed 2016-17 as the 'Year of Cultural Heritage' to promote the region's shared cultural legacy.

q: 34. Where is the head quarter of SAARC Chamber of commerce and industry located?
explain: The SAARC Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) has its headquarters in Islamabad, Pakistan.

q: 35. Where is SAARC cultural centre located?
explain: The SAARC Cultural Centre is located in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

q: 36. Comparing the following Regional Centers established in the SAARC nations; choose the correct answer from the code. a.Nepal b.Bangladesh c.India d.Pakistan / 1.Agricultural Centre(SAC) 2.Environment & Natural Disaster(END) 3.Energy Centre(SEC) 4.Tuberculosis Centre(STC)
explain: Nepal hosts the Tuberculosis Centre (STC), Bangladesh hosts the Agricultural Centre (SAC), India hosts the Environment & Natural Disaster centre (END), and Pakistan hosts the Energy Centre (SEC): a-4, b-1, c-2, d-3.

q: 37. How many Country/Organization that granted for the observer status of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC has granted observer status to 9 countries/organizations, including Australia, China, EU, Iran, Japan, South Korea, Mauritius, Myanmar, and the USA.

q: 38. Which of the following SAARC country with highest population literacy rate?
explain: Maldives has the highest literacy rate among SAARC nations, close to universal literacy.

q: 39. When was BIMSTEC established?
explain: BIMSTEC was established on 6 June 1997 through the Bangkok Declaration.

q: 40. Which of the following statement is/are correct?
options: Nepal was granted the observer status of BIMSTEC in 1998
In 2018, it was expanded to embrace two more sectors including blue economy and mountain economy
Now, it has 7 areas of cooperation
explain: All three statements are correct: Nepal held observer status before becoming a full member, the sectors were expanded in 2018, and BIMSTEC now has 7 broad areas of cooperation.

q: 41. What is the regional initiative comprising 7 member states of both SAARC and ASEAN called?
explain: BIMSTEC brings together countries bridging South Asia (SAARC) and Southeast Asia (ASEAN) around the Bay of Bengal.

q: 42. At the conclusion of the 6th BIMSTEC summit, ___ took over as chair nation of BIMSTEC.
explain: Bangladesh assumed the BIMSTEC chairmanship at the conclusion of the 6th Summit in Bangkok.

q: 43. Which country was hosted the sixth BIMSTEC Summit in 2025?
explain: Thailand hosted the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in Bangkok in 2025.
